name: Tufted Puffin
rangeDescription: Coasts and islands of northeastern asia to aleutians and southern california
description: The largest puffin, this chunky seabird has an entirely black body, white face, and fetching tuft of yellowish feathers curling around its nape. Thick orange bill and orange feet.

name: Somali Ostrich
rangeDescription: Desert to savanna plains of northeastern africa, from northern ethiopia, djibouti, and somalia southward through far southeastern south sudan, and southeastern kenya
description: A long-legged and long-necked flightless bird. Males have a blue-gray neck and legs, but the bill and front of the legs become pink when breeding.

name: Indigo Flowerpiercer
rangeDescription: Andes of western colombia and northwestern ecuador (southward to pichincha)
description: Small flowerpiercer with restricted range in western Colombia and northwest Ecuador. Entirely ultramarine blue, though can appear dark in poor light.

name: Eastern Dwarf Hornbill
rangeDescription: Congo basin of central african republic to democratic republic of the congo and uganda
description: A small, dark forest hornbill found predominantly in primary forest subcanopy, where it prefers areas with abundant vines. This species is unique in its overall dark coloration and its broad white eyebrow that extends to the back of the head.

name: White-throated Antpitta
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru and western bolivia to far northwestern argentina
description: Plump bicolored bird with long gray legs. Brown above and light gray below, with an orange-red head, a white throat, and a white eye-ring.

name: Carunculated Caracara
rangeDescription: Páramo of southwestern colombia and ecuador
description: Strikingly patterned raptor of the high Andes in Ecuador and southern Colombia. Note pied plumage pattern, white streaks on black breast, and orange face.

name: Sombre Pigeon
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of sulawesi
description: A distinctive, very large gray pigeon with a small patch of red skin around the eye and a barred belly and undertail. Back blackish-gray, head and breast much paler gray.

name: Emin's Shrike
rangeDescription: Ivory coast to south sudan, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, and northern uganda
description: A small, attractive shrike with a rufous back and rump, a gray cap and neck, and a black mask through the eyes. Usually shows a small white patch on the front of the wing.

name: Peruvian Martin
rangeDescription: Coastal peru (piura southward to ica), rarely to northern chile (arica)
description: Scarce, local, and poorly known large swallow of lowland deserts and coastal areas. Usually seen as singles or small groups, usually apart from other swallows.

name: Rufous-chested Dotterel
rangeDescription: Breeds southern chile (north to chiloé) and southern argentina to tierra del fuego and falkland islands; winters north to northern chile and southeastern brazil
description: A handsome, distinctive, and medium-sized plover that breeds on southern moorland and steppe, and migrates north to winter on beaches and coastal flats. Found mainly in pairs and small loose groups in summer, but migrant and winter flocks can be a few hundred birds.

name: Manus Cicadabird
rangeDescription: Manus island (admiralty islands)
description: Male is dark slate-gray with a black tail tip, black wing feathers, and a dark blackish mask. Female is gray-capped, cinnamon below with distinct barring, and brownish above.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: White-winged Coot
rangeDescription: Far southeastern brazil to eastern bolivia and southward to tierra del fuego
description: Fairly common to uncommon coot, mainly in lowlands. Found on fresh to brackish ponds and lakes and wetlands with open water.

name: Angola Helmetshrike
rangeDescription: Western angola (gabela escarpment)
description: A gregarious, cartoonish, mostly gray-brown helmetshrike with a black head, piercing orange eyes, red legs and eye-wattles, and an orange-tipped red bill. Pairs and flocks of 4–10 inhabit mature dry and secondary forest, plantations, and thickets in a narrow range along the Angolan escarpment, where it is endemic and endangered.

name: Visayan Fantail
rangeDescription: Philippines (guimaras, masbate, negros, panay, and ticao)
description: A medium-sized, long-tailed bird of forest from the lowlands to low elevations in the mountains in the west-central Philippines. Dull blue on the head, chest, back, and shoulder, with some paler blue streaking on the chest and crown.

name: Patagonian Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southern chile (valdivia) and adjacent argentina southward to tierra del fuego
description: Rather plain but subtly attractive little flycatcher best known in migration and winter, when it occurs widely in gardens, parks, and open woodlands, often with fruiting shrubs. In summer, inhabits temperate native rainforest where it often stays rather high in the trees and is easily overlooked.

name: Coal-crested Finch
rangeDescription: Campos of northeastern bolivia to northeastern and central brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Handsome finch with a spiky crest. Males have a black band from the head to the center of the belly, a silver back, and brown-yellow underparts.

name: Humboldt Penguin
rangeDescription: Humboldt current region of coastal northern peru to southern chile
description: Uncommon and local; breeds in colonies along the coast of Peru and Chile, where it nests in underground burrows. The only penguin in most of its range, but some overlap in central Chile with similar Magellanic Penguin of colder southern waters.

name: Orange-throated Sunangel
rangeDescription: Andes of northeastern colombia to northwestern venezuela (southern lara to táchira)
description: Medium-sized hummingbird with a short, straight bill found in the Andes of Venezuela and eastern Colombia. Male has a green body, buff and green spotted underparts, and a glittering orange throat.

name: Eastern Shrike-tit
rangeDescription: Southeastern australia (central queensland to southern victoria and southeastern south australia)
description: Small bird with short, heavy bill. Green above, yellow below, with bold black-and-white head pattern.

name: Nuttall's Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Chaparral and oak woodland of northern california to northwestern baja
description: Small woodpecker almost entirely restricted to the state of California (barely entering northern Baja). Look for black-and-white barring on the back and patterned flanks.
